shortDescription: Women’s sustainable fashion brand Reformation NYSE:REF marked its first earnings report as a publicly traded company with better-than-expected results and its 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth."Reformation is beginning its public company journey from a position of strength,” s…

children: as a publicly traded company with better-than-expected results and its 21st consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

"Reformation is beginning its public company journey from a position of strength,” said CEO Hali Borenstein, adding that the consistency of the company’s results reflects “the enduring strength of the brand, agile merchandising model, and disciplined execution.”

The company not only realized double-digit growth in net sales but also a 21.2% jump in DTC revenue and a 48.7% gain in wholesale revenue, all of which contributed to a 79.4% surge in net income to $12.4M, or $0.23 per share, beating expectations by a penny.
Active customers increased 22.9%, reflecting strength across customer retention and new customer acquisition.
By region, U.S. sales were up 21.4%, while international sales rose 36.8% thanks to the company’s expansion across France.
The gains coupled with lower tariff rates and higher average unit retail helped expand Reformation’s
gross margin by 230 basis points to 66.7%.
Looking ahead to the rest of the year, Reformation
sees revenue increasing by 18.6% to 19.5%, representing a range of $602M to $606M versus $601.33M estimates. Adjusted EBITDA margin is seen within a range of 14% and 14.2%.
also plans to spend $23M to $27M tied to the opening of 15 to 16 new stores in FY26.
Shares are higher in after-hours trading.

title: Reformation's first public quarter delivers double-digit growth, an upbeat outlook
